mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (5.4→7.7→9.9→9.0) signals normalization of essential-goods purchasing patterns. This normalization reduces friction in retail supply chains and consumer confidence, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose monotonically from t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverses by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (7.4→5.3→4.1→3.7) indicates accelerating return to out-of-home activity. This behavioral shift, sustained over four weeks, directly increases retail-and-recreation foot traffic as consumers exit residential confinement.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility stabilizes or increases in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC fails to rise in at least 3 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -20.0 to -14.3 over four weeks. When WORKPLACES recovery exceeds -15 percentage points AND TRANSIT remains below -15 points, commuters shift to personal retail trips during off-peak hours, increasing RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -14.3 in t-0w, TRANSIT at -15.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -15 points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC declines despite WORKPLACES remaining above -15.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -9.3 to +4.7 over four weeks, signaling relaxation of outdoor-activity restrictions. This policy shift enables weekend retail-and-recreation activity to expand, producing higher RETAIL_REC in the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS crossed zero between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below zero in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of WORKPLACES (-14.3) and TRANSIT (-15.7) deficits signals a regime where commuting is partially restored but transit-dependent trips remain suppressed. Consumers compensate by clustering retail visits with workplace trips, increasing RETAIL_REC intensity per outing.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT gap narrowed from 3.9 to 1.4 points
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT gap widens beyond 3 points, or RETAIL_REC declines in 3 or more of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility at +4.7 indicates seasonal outdoor-activity peak. This peak correlates with retail-adjacent behaviors (outdoor dining, shopping districts). RETAIL_REC will rise in the next week as consumers exploit favorable conditions.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility falls below +2 in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved from -22.7 to -16.4 over four weeks, a 6.3-point recovery. This momentum, combined with GROCERY_PHARM stability above +9, indicates sustained consumer engagement. Inertia in this trajectory produces further RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6.3 points over four weeks, GROCERY_PHARM stable at 9.0-9.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses by more than 2 points in week t+1, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below +6 while RETAIL_REC continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility deficit (-15.7) persists despite WORKPLACES recovery, indicating policy-driven transit constraints remain. Consumers substitute transit with personal retail trips, but only if RESIDENTIAL mobility continues declining. This three-way interaction drives RETAIL_REC higher over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:All three conditions met in t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 4 in week t+1, or TRANSIT recovers above -15 without corresponding RETAIL_REC gains, or RETAIL_REC declines in both weeks t+1 and t+2.
